- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day); cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; apply downward correction of 2–5% on next forecast.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 60–70% of 30d range); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- For 30d horizon, model often lags 1–2 days behind true trend; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is consistently 1.00 (strong bullish) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overbought bias.
